newsitem.title: CANADA: North and Central America port conditions - Lloyds.
newsitem.headline: North and Central America port conditions - Lloyds.

text.p: Port conditions from Lloyds Shipping Intelligence Service --

CANADA, October 28 - Vancouver - GRAIN - 4 vessels loading, 9 waiting, with waiting time of 5-7 days. 22 Vessels due by 11/11. Roberts Bank - COAL - 2 Vessels loading, 22 due to load in November. Prince Rupert - GRAIN - 3 Vessels awaiting cargo, waiting time of 7-10 days. Halifax, SC - All terminals operating normally. No delays at container terminals. Breakbulk piers have space available. No delays at bunker and tanker facilities. Pier 9b closed for repairs which are expected to be completed by summer 1997. Reconstruction of pier 26/27 expected to be completed by January 1997 to include resurfacing and shed to specialise in forest products.

HONDURAS, October 28 - Puerto Cortes - Vessels berthed, 2 discharging/loading contairs, 1 loading bananas/discharging containers, 1 discharging general cargo, 1 loading bananas, 1 U.S. navy vessel discharging. General cargo vessels awaiting berth, 3 to discharge/load containers, 1 to load/discharge. Generals vessels due, 5 to discharge/load containers, 4 to discharge/load generals, 5 to load bananas, 1 to discharge bagged soda ash. Three berthed of which 2 discharging/loading containers, 1 loading bananas. 14 vessels due of which 8 to discharge/load containers, 5 to load bananas, 1 to discharge paper products. No delays expected.

MEXICO, October 29 - Tampico - Vessels in port, 1 sugar, 2 general cargo, 1 steel coils, 1 lead, 1 steel bars. Working normally. Altamira - Vessels in port, 2 minerals, 1 under repair. Working normally. Veracruz - Vessels in port, 2 sugar, 1 pipes, 2 containers, 3 corn, 3 grain, 1 palm oil. Working normally. Manzanillo - Vessels in port, 2 containers, 2 chemicals, 3 general cargo, 1 cars, 1 under repair. Working normally. Coatzacoalcos - Vessels in port, 10 chemicals, 7 oil tanker. Working normally.

PANAMA, October 28 - Balboa - One tanker in port operating. Cristobal - One tanker and 1 container carrier operating. Panama Canal - Working to full capacity. Lane outages are scheduled at Miraflores and Gatun locks simultaneously from 5/11 to 9/11 for maintenance and repairs. Transit capacity should average 28-30 vessels per day during this period. Availability of the transit booking system will be assessed pursuant to provisions of marine director's notice to shipping no. n-7-95. As of 28/10, 27 vessels due, 16 in queue, 7 booked, 37 scheduled.

UNITED STATES, October 28 - Hampton Roads, VA - Five general cargo/container vessels operating, 4 bulkers in pier loading, 4 anchored, 1 bulker loading fertiliser. 1 Under repair and/or layberth. 1 Tanker discharging crude, 1 bulker discharging minerals. Baltimore, MD - Vessels operating in port 6 bulkers, 4 container 2 ro/ro, 2 auto, 3 general. 2 Cable vessels on standby, 2 vessels in repair yard, 2 bulkers awaiting berth, 1 to discharge sugar. Jersey City, NJ - one vessel in port. Port Elizabeth, NJ - Four in port. Perth Amboy, NJ - One in port. Cartaret - One in port. Port Newark, Bayway, NJ - No vessels. Baltimore, MD - No congestion at Dundalk terminal, no adverse conditions at C,D canal/Baltimore harbour low ceiling. Elevators and coal operations no delays. Average waiting time Consol Coal 5 days. Liquid bulk facilities normal, no congestion. Anchorage clear at Baltimore and Annapolis.

Charleston, SC - Light vessel traffic at Columbus St terminal. Congestion expected at Wando terminal in early part of week. No delays at oil terminals/grain elevator. Harbour pilots announced vessels calling at Wando Welch and Columbus St terminal will be allowed to proceed to berth at a depth up to 38 ft. No delays expected. Jacksonville - No heavy berth congestion or delays or at Fernandina Beach, FL. Miami, FL - No congestion at port, all berths available for cargo operations. New York, NY - No congestion at anchorages, container, sugar or tanker terminals. Norfolk, VA - 13 Vessels due at Norfolk Southern Coal pier this week, 7 at Dominion terminal, 5 anchored waiting to load, 4 due at Pier IX coal terminal, no vessels due at Cargill. Container and general cargo terminals working normally, no delays. Oil and bulk terminals working normally, all channels opening with prevailing depths available.

Philadelphia, PA - No congestion, or at Camden, Wilmington. Savannah, GA - No congestion at Georgia Ports Authorities Garden City terminals and Ocean terminals, no bulk congestion. No delays at Colonial Marine. Afternoon thundershowers, weather sensitive cargo may expect downtime. Possible delays due to fog, navigational conditions remain normal. Gulf Coast Houston, TX - No congestion at city docks, Galveston grain elevators but congestion in some oil/chemical terminals. Mobile, AL - Terminals working normally, No congestion expected. New Orleans, LA - Rain can cause delays in cargo operations, especially grain loading. River stage 4.8 ft, normal transit times expected. Bar pilots advise Saturday and Sunday draft for Mississippi River Gulf outlet will be 30 ft. Present max permissible draft at SWASS 47 ft fw for vessels under 100,000 dwt, 46 ft over 100,000 dwt. Some elevators not working weekends due to slower than usual grain shipments.

West Coast, Columbia River - 10 Grain vessels in Columbia river district, 5 loading, 5 waiting. Coos Bay - Normal. Two woodchip vessels loading, 1 log/1 lumber vessel due, no delays. Honolulu, HI - Heavy south swell off harbour prevented several vessels from bunkering offport in past week. Conditions expected to improve during coming week. Long Beach - Metropolitan moderately heavy for November. 1-2 Days delay at anchor awaiting berth. Koch carbon - 1 Vessel due in November. Kaiser berthing delays 1-2 days for coal/petcoke. Moderate in Los Angeles/Long Beach harbour for bulk cargoes. Seattle - Both grain elevators have backlog at anchor awaiting berth, 39 reefers on line up to call Seattle for bulk apples.
